reviews.title: Great wired headset - excellent for gaming and work
reviews.comment: My old Plantronics (10 years+) started to give me bad feedback and noise, especially when using the mic. So it was time for a new headset. I wanted something I could use for work and for gaming with my PC. Wireless was not important to me, but I wanted a more comfortable feeling, a very good mic/noise cancelling mic, and good sound quality.  I also did not want to spend $200. After searching and researching I settled on the Corsair HS60. I was iffy on it - some of the reviews here were 'meh' and 'not good' and 'broken out of the box' but on sale for $120ish I figured if they weren't any good I could always return them. They came really fast and I were basically Plug & Play. My RAM is also Corsair and the headset works with ICUE but the headset doesn't have RGB lights. I'd have to look into this feature more to see what the headset can do with it. I bring it up because when I plugged in the headset, it wanted me to update the software. Anyway - the headset installed and needed a reboot, and then worked perfectly. The headset is one of the most comfortable I've ever used, it's comfort is leaps ahead on my Plantronics and tiny Logitech headset I use at work. The sound quality is very good, and it's volume range is robust. So far, the mic has been working as I need it, I've used it in over ten work meetings and five gaming sessions, and other than moving the mic closer to my mouth there have been zero feedback complaints or background noise pickups. The headset has some decent noise-reduction, I can't hear my dog whining or my girlfriend crying for help when she drops something unless it's really big/glass. I didn't buy the headset for the haptic response, although it is a cool feature for gaming. I do appreciate I can control how much of the effect comes through. I don't mind that they're wired - since I'm using them at my work/gaming PC. The only thing I hate about them - it only comes in this camo pattern/color. It is not my aesthetic. Lastly, I think there are well worth the $100+, I'd say they are somewhere "well above" your generic $20-60 headset. If you needs are similar to mine, I would highly recommend this headset.
reviews.author: Justinian

reviews.title: Best Gaming Headphones Ever!
reviews.comment: My son loves this gaming headphone set. These offer crystal clear sound, are noise cancelling, and make you feel like you are part of whatever game you are playing. He has only ever used the Corsair Haptics and loves them. They last a very long time too!!!
reviews.author: Rebecca

reviews.title: great sound, cheap ear cushions
reviews.comment: I've purchased this headset about 3 times over the last 5 or 6 years and I'm currently using logitech pros and i miss the corsairs - the only caveat is the ear cushions are made of super cheap material and start degrading after a 6 months to a year, leaving little black specs on your skin and all over your desk. You can purchase off brand replacement ear cushions but they compromise sound.. definitely a great headset tho, make sure you turn the bass up on the side of the headset and listen to your favorite song - you wont regret it :)
reviews.author: Justin

reviews.title: Ramen-Fueled Gaming Bliss: Corsair HS60 HAPTIC Takes Me on a Bass-Boosted Ride!
reviews.comment: Yo, fellow gamers! I'm here to spill the deets on the Corsair HS60 HAPTIC Stereo Gaming Headset with Haptic Bass, and let me tell ya, it's like I've found the ultimate gaming companion without even leavin' my ramen nest. This thing's got more vibes than my gaming rig's RGB lighting! First off, this headset's like a soft cloud huggin' my ears – no joke, I could be in an intense raid for hours and my ears feel cozier than my bed after a gaming marathon. And let's talk bass, man. The haptic bass ain't no wimpy shake – it's like a full-blown bass drop right on my dome, bringin' my game explosions to life in a way that even my trusty instant ramen can't top. Now, I ain't no audiophile, but the sound quality's so crisp I swear I can hear my opponents rage-quittin' across the server. Footsteps, gunshots, even the distant cries of my hunger pangs – this headset picks 'em all up like I've got supersonic ears or somethin'. And the noise cancellation's like puttin' up a "Do Not Disturb" sign to the outside world, keepin' my gaming bubble sacred. And let's talk about the haptic part. It's like the headset's givin' me a friendly pat on the back every time I land a headshot or pull off a slick move. It's like my own personal victory dance without even gettin' outta my chair! Plus, the haptic bass syncs up with my game's explosions and thumps, makin' me feel like I'm in the middle of the action – ramen bowl and all. Now, I know I ain't the healthiest eater, but even I can appreciate this headset's comfort. It's like wearin' a pair of fluffy pillows on my ears, even when I'm rockin' the headset through marathon gaming sessions fueled by my stash of ramen noodles. My ears stay comfy even if my posture's a mess. All in all, the Corsair HS60 HAPTIC Stereo Gaming Headset's my trusty sidekick in my quest to conquer digital worlds without leavin' my ramen lair. If you're lookin' for a headset that'll make your game vibes hit harder than a midnight snack attack, this one's a no-brainer. Five stars? Nah, this headset deserves a high score that goes off the charts!
reviews.author: Allenzon

reviews.title: Great...until it falls apart
reviews.comment: I purchased this item almost exactly one year ago.  I owned a headset with the same technology from kickstarter and was looking for something a bit more comfortable.  I heard that the same company was working with Corsair so I jumped at the chance to get my hands on these.  I do find the headset to be comfortable and the sound quality is solid.  While these headphones don't quite pack the same punch as the ones from kickstarter I still love the taction technology in these.  All that being said I'm sitting here a year later and the leather is all fraying, The bracket on one side of my headset has broken and now the ear piece just dangles.  I don't expect headphones in this price range to last forever, but only a year to me is unacceptable for someone that takes care of their equipment.
reviews.author: Luigi
